about: Sakila workload for tools/sample_db_bench.py. origin 'upstream-view': the 7 CREATE VIEW bodies of upstream/sakila-mv-schema.sql (name = upstream view name), adapted from MySQL to BigQuery SQL as 'adaptation' says; 'upstream-procedure': the SELECTs of the stored procedures and functions of the same script (film_in_stock, film_not_in_stock, rewards_report, get_customer_balance, inventory_held_by_customer, inventory_in_stock) with their parameters bound to the values 'adaptation' names; 'authored': written for this eval. Sakila ships no test queries. Views are also created in DuckDB (create_view), as upstream creates them.

queries.name: customer_list
queries.adaptation: IF(cu.active, ...) becomes IF(cu.active = 1, ...) (active is INT64 holding 0 or 1, see the adapted DDL); the _utf8 character-set introducers are dropped
queries.sql:
SELECT cu.customer_id AS ID, CONCAT(cu.first_name, ' ', cu.last_name) AS name, a.address AS address, a.postal_code AS `zip code`,
  a.phone AS phone, city.city AS city, country.country AS country, IF(cu.active = 1, 'active', '') AS notes, cu.store_id AS SID
FROM customer AS cu JOIN address AS a ON cu.address_id = a.address_id JOIN city ON a.city_id = city.city_id
  JOIN country ON city.country_id = country.country_id

queries.name: film_list
queries.adaptation: GROUP_CONCAT(x SEPARATOR ', ') becomes STRING_AGG(x, ', ' ORDER BY actor.actor_id) (MySQL leaves the order unspecified; the ORDER BY makes the result deterministic); the columns MySQL accepts because they depend on film.film_id are added to GROUP BY, as BigQuery requires; _utf8 introducers dropped
queries.sql:
SELECT film.film_id AS FID, film.title AS title, film.description AS description, category.name AS category, film.rental_rate AS price,
  film.length AS length, film.rating AS rating, STRING_AGG(CONCAT(actor.first_name, ' ', actor.last_name), ', ' ORDER BY actor.actor_id) AS actors
FROM category LEFT JOIN film_category ON category.category_id = film_category.category_id LEFT JOIN film ON film_category.film_id = film.film_id
  JOIN film_actor ON film.film_id = film_actor.film_id
  JOIN actor ON film_actor.actor_id = actor.actor_id
GROUP BY film.film_id, category.name, film.title, film.description, film.rental_rate, film.length, film.rating

queries.name: nicer_but_slower_film_list
queries.adaptation: as film_list: STRING_AGG with an ORDER BY, the dependent columns added to GROUP BY; UCASE and LCASE become UPPER and LOWER, _utf8 introducers dropped
queries.sql:
SELECT film.film_id AS FID, film.title AS title, film.description AS description, category.name AS category, film.rental_rate AS price,
  film.length AS length, film.rating AS rating, STRING_AGG(CONCAT(CONCAT(UPPER(SUBSTR(actor.first_name, 1, 1)),
  LOWER(SUBSTR(actor.first_name, 2, LENGTH(actor.first_name))), ' ', CONCAT(UPPER(SUBSTR(actor.last_name, 1, 1)),
  LOWER(SUBSTR(actor.last_name, 2, LENGTH(actor.last_name)))))), ', ' ORDER BY actor.actor_id) AS actors
FROM category LEFT JOIN film_category ON category.category_id = film_category.category_id LEFT JOIN film ON film_category.film_id = film.film_id
  JOIN film_actor ON film.film_id = film_actor.film_id
  JOIN actor ON film_actor.actor_id = actor.actor_id
GROUP BY film.film_id, category.name, film.title, film.description, film.rental_rate, film.length, film.rating

queries.name: staff_list
queries.sql:
SELECT s.staff_id AS ID, CONCAT(s.first_name, ' ', s.last_name) AS name, a.address AS address, a.postal_code AS `zip code`, a.phone AS phone,
  city.city AS city, country.country AS country, s.store_id AS SID
FROM staff AS s JOIN address AS a ON s.address_id = a.address_id JOIN city ON a.city_id = city.city_id
  JOIN country ON city.country_id = country.country_id

queries.name: sales_by_store
queries.adaptation: the columns that depend on s.store_id are added to GROUP BY (BigQuery needs them; MySQL groups by s.store_id alone); _utf8 introducers dropped
queries.sql:
SELECT
CONCAT(c.city, ',', cy.country) AS store
, CONCAT(m.first_name, ' ', m.last_name) AS manager
, SUM(p.amount) AS total_sales
FROM payment AS p
INNER JOIN rental AS r ON p.rental_id = r.rental_id
INNER JOIN inventory AS i ON r.inventory_id = i.inventory_id
INNER JOIN store AS s ON i.store_id = s.store_id
INNER JOIN address AS a ON s.address_id = a.address_id
INNER JOIN city AS c ON a.city_id = c.city_id
INNER JOIN country AS cy ON c.country_id = cy.country_id
INNER JOIN staff AS m ON s.manager_staff_id = m.staff_id
GROUP BY s.store_id, c.city, cy.country, m.first_name, m.last_name
ORDER BY cy.country, c.city

queries.name: sales_by_film_category
queries.sql:
SELECT
c.name AS category
, SUM(p.amount) AS total_sales
FROM payment AS p
INNER JOIN rental AS r ON p.rental_id = r.rental_id
INNER JOIN inventory AS i ON r.inventory_id = i.inventory_id
INNER JOIN film AS f ON i.film_id = f.film_id
INNER JOIN film_category AS fc ON f.film_id = fc.film_id
INNER JOIN category AS c ON fc.category_id = c.category_id
GROUP BY c.name
ORDER BY total_sales DESC

queries.name: actor_info
queries.adaptation: GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT CONCAT(c.name, ': ', (subquery)) ORDER BY c.name SEPARATOR '; ') becomes STRING_AGG(DISTINCT x, '; ' ORDER BY x) over a derived table that computes x: BigQuery and DuckDB need the ORDER BY of a DISTINCT aggregate to be the aggregated expression (x starts with c.name, so the order is the same), and the correlated subquery moves into the derived table; the sakila. schema prefixes are dropped
queries.sql:
SELECT t.actor_id, t.first_name, t.last_name,
  STRING_AGG(DISTINCT t.category_films, '; ' ORDER BY t.category_films) AS film_info
FROM (
  SELECT
  a.actor_id,
  a.first_name,
  a.last_name,
  CONCAT(c.name, ': ',
    (SELECT STRING_AGG(f.title, ', ' ORDER BY f.title)
        FROM film AS f
        INNER JOIN film_category AS fc
          ON f.film_id = fc.film_id
        INNER JOIN film_actor AS fa
          ON f.film_id = fa.film_id
        WHERE fc.category_id = c.category_id
        AND fa.actor_id = a.actor_id
     )) AS category_films
  FROM actor AS a
  LEFT JOIN film_actor AS fa
    ON a.actor_id = fa.actor_id
  LEFT JOIN film_category AS fc
    ON fa.film_id = fc.film_id
  LEFT JOIN category AS c
    ON fc.category_id = c.category_id
) AS t
GROUP BY t.actor_id, t.first_name, t.last_name

queries.adaptation: rewards_report: the INSERT ... SELECT that fills tmpCustomer; parameters bound: min_monthly_purchases = 6, min_dollar_amount_purchased = 40.00, last_month_start = 2005-07-01 and last_month_end = 2005-07-31 (the procedure derives both from CURRENT_DATE, which has no rentals in this data)
queries.sql:
SELECT p.customer_id
FROM payment AS p
WHERE DATE(p.payment_date) BETWEEN DATE '2005-07-01' AND DATE '2005-07-31'
GROUP BY customer_id
HAVING SUM(p.amount) > 40.00
AND COUNT(customer_id) > 6

queries.adaptation: rewards_report: the final SELECT over tmpCustomer; the temporary table tmpCustomer is inlined as the derived table that fills it; parameters bound as in rewards-report-customers
queries.sql:
SELECT c.*
FROM (
  SELECT p.customer_id
  FROM payment AS p
  WHERE DATE(p.payment_date) BETWEEN DATE '2005-07-01' AND DATE '2005-07-31'
  GROUP BY customer_id
  HAVING SUM(p.amount) > 40.00
  AND COUNT(customer_id) > 6
) AS t
INNER JOIN customer AS c ON t.customer_id = c.customer_id

queries.adaptation: film_in_stock: the SELECT; parameters bound: p_film_id = 1, p_store_id = 1; the stored function inventory_in_stock(inventory_id) is inlined as NOT EXISTS (a rental of the item with no return_date), which is what its body computes
queries.sql:
SELECT inventory_id
FROM inventory
WHERE film_id = 1
AND store_id = 1
AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM rental AS r WHERE r.inventory_id = inventory.inventory_id AND r.return_date IS NULL)

queries.adaptation: film_not_in_stock: the SELECT; parameters bound: p_film_id = 2, p_store_id = 2; NOT inventory_in_stock(inventory_id) is inlined as EXISTS (a rental of the item with no return_date)
queries.sql:
SELECT inventory_id
FROM inventory
WHERE film_id = 2
AND store_id = 2
AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM rental AS r WHERE r.inventory_id = inventory.inventory_id AND r.return_date IS NULL)

queries.adaptation: get_customer_balance: rental fees; parameters bound: p_customer_id = 130, p_effective_date = 2005-08-01
queries.sql:
SELECT IFNULL(SUM(film.rental_rate), 0)
FROM film, inventory, rental
WHERE film.film_id = inventory.film_id
AND inventory.inventory_id = rental.inventory_id
AND rental.rental_date <= DATETIME '2005-08-01 00:00:00'
AND rental.customer_id = 130

queries.adaptation: get_customer_balance: late fees; parameters bound as in customer-balance-rental-fees; TO_DAYS(a) - TO_DAYS(b) becomes DATE_DIFF(DATE(a), DATE(b), DAY)
queries.sql:
SELECT IFNULL(SUM(IF(DATE_DIFF(DATE(rental.return_date), DATE(rental.rental_date), DAY) > film.rental_duration,
      DATE_DIFF(DATE(rental.return_date), DATE(rental.rental_date), DAY) - film.rental_duration, 0)), 0)
FROM rental, inventory, film
WHERE film.film_id = inventory.film_id
AND inventory.inventory_id = rental.inventory_id
AND rental.rental_date <= DATETIME '2005-08-01 00:00:00'
AND rental.customer_id = 130

queries.adaptation: get_customer_balance: payments made; parameters bound as in customer-balance-rental-fees
queries.sql:
SELECT IFNULL(SUM(payment.amount), 0)
FROM payment
WHERE payment.payment_date <= DATETIME '2005-08-01 00:00:00'
AND payment.customer_id = 130

queries.sql:
SELECT customer_id
FROM rental
WHERE return_date IS NULL

queries.sql:

queries.adaptation: inventory_in_stock: the count of rentals still out; parameter bound: p_inventory_id = 2047
queries.sql:
SELECT COUNT(rental_id)
FROM inventory LEFT JOIN rental USING (inventory_id)
WHERE inventory.inventory_id = 2047
AND rental.return_date IS NULL

SELECT f.film_id, f.title, l.name AS language, c.name AS category
FROM film AS f
JOIN language AS l ON l.language_id = f.language_id
JOIN film_category AS fc ON fc.film_id = f.film_id
JOIN category AS c ON c.category_id = fc.category_id
WHERE f.rating = 'PG'

SELECT p.payment_id, p.amount, r.rental_id
FROM payment AS p
LEFT JOIN rental AS r ON r.rental_id = p.rental_id
WHERE r.rental_id IS NULL

SELECT a1.actor_id AS first_id, a2.actor_id AS second_id, a1.last_name
FROM actor AS a1
JOIN actor AS a2 ON a1.last_name = a2.last_name AND a1.actor_id < a2.actor_id

SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS rentals
FROM rental
GROUP BY customer_id
HAVING COUNT(*) > 35

SELECT DISTINCT film_id, title, rental_rate
FROM film

SELECT DISTINCT ci.city, co.country
FROM customer AS c
JOIN address AS a ON a.address_id = c.address_id
JOIN city AS ci ON ci.city_id = a.city_id
JOIN country AS co ON co.country_id = ci.country_id

SELECT title
FROM film
WHERE film_id IN (SELECT film_id FROM inventory WHERE store_id = 1)

SELECT c.customer_id, c.last_name
FROM customer AS c
WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM payment AS p WHERE p.customer_id = c.customer_id AND p.amount > 10)

SELECT f.film_id, f.title
FROM film AS f
WHERE NOT EXISTS (
  SELECT 1 FROM inventory AS i JOIN rental AS r ON r.inventory_id = i.inventory_id WHERE i.film_id = f.film_id
)

SELECT payment_id
FROM payment
WHERE rental_id NOT IN (SELECT rental_id FROM rental WHERE customer_id = 1)

SELECT film_id, title, rental_rate
FROM film
WHERE rental_rate > (SELECT AVG(rental_rate) FROM film)

SELECT c.customer_id,
  (SELECT MAX(r.rental_date) FROM rental AS r WHERE r.customer_id = c.customer_id) AS last_rental
FROM customer AS c

SELECT email FROM customer
UNION ALL
SELECT email FROM staff

SELECT a.city_id FROM customer AS c JOIN address AS a ON a.address_id = c.address_id
UNION DISTINCT
SELECT a.city_id FROM staff AS s JOIN address AS a ON a.address_id = s.address_id

SELECT actor_id FROM film_actor WHERE film_id = 1
INTERSECT DISTINCT
SELECT actor_id FROM film_actor WHERE film_id = 23

SELECT category_id FROM category
EXCEPT DISTINCT
SELECT fc.category_id FROM film_category AS fc JOIN film AS f ON f.film_id = fc.film_id WHERE f.length > 180

SELECT film_id, rating, length,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY rating ORDER BY length DESC) AS length_rank,
  DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY rating ORDER BY length DESC) AS length_dense_rank
FROM film

SELECT payment_id, customer_id, amount,
  amount - LAG(amount) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY payment_date, payment_id) AS change
FROM payment

SELECT payment_id, customer_id,
  SUM(amount) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY payment_date, payment_id ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS running
FROM payment

SELECT film_id, title
FROM film
WHERE (rating = 'G') AND 1 = 1 AND TRUE AND (((length > 100)))

SELECT t.store_id, t.n
FROM (SELECT store_id, COUNT(*) AS n FROM inventory WHERE 1 = 1 GROUP BY store_id) AS t
WHERE t.n > 0

SELECT c.name, totals.revenue
FROM category AS c
JOIN (
  SELECT fc.category_id, SUM(p.amount) AS revenue
  FROM payment AS p
  JOIN rental AS r ON r.rental_id = p.rental_id
  JOIN inventory AS i ON i.inventory_id = r.inventory_id
  JOIN film_category AS fc ON fc.film_id = i.film_id
  GROUP BY fc.category_id
) AS totals ON totals.category_id = c.category_id
WHERE totals.revenue > 4800

SELECT i.store_id, COUNTIF(r.return_date IS NULL) AS unreturned, COUNT(*) AS rentals
FROM rental AS r
JOIN inventory AS i ON i.inventory_id = r.inventory_id
GROUP BY i.store_id

SELECT f.film_id, i.inventory_id
FROM film AS f
LEFT JOIN inventory AS i ON i.film_id = f.film_id AND i.store_id = 1
WHERE f.rating = 'G'

SELECT fa.film_id, a.actor_id
FROM film_actor AS fa
RIGHT JOIN actor AS a ON a.actor_id = fa.actor_id AND fa.film_id <= 10

SELECT c.category_id, fc.film_id
FROM category AS c
FULL OUTER JOIN film_category AS fc ON fc.category_id = c.category_id AND fc.film_id < 20

SELECT fa.actor_id, COUNT(DISTINCT fc.category_id) AS categories
FROM film_actor AS fa
JOIN film_category AS fc ON fc.film_id = fa.film_id
GROUP BY fa.actor_id
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT fc.category_id) >= 15

SELECT s.store_id, m.last_name, COUNT(*) AS items
FROM store AS s
JOIN staff AS m ON m.staff_id = s.manager_staff_id
JOIN inventory AS i ON i.store_id = s.store_id
GROUP BY s.store_id, m.last_name, s.manager_staff_id

SELECT customer_id, COALESCE(email, 'none') AS contact, CASE WHEN email IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END AS has_email
FROM customer

SELECT EXTRACT(YEAR FROM rental_date) AS y, EXTRACT(MONTH FROM rental_date) AS m, COUNT(*) AS rentals
FROM rental
GROUP BY y, m

SELECT customer_id, SUM(amount) AS spent
FROM payment
GROUP BY customer_id
ORDER BY spent DESC, customer_id
LIMIT 10

SELECT film_id, title
FROM film
WHERE rating IN ('G', 'PG') AND length BETWEEN 60 AND 90

SELECT film_id, UPPER(title) AS upper_title, LENGTH(title) AS title_length
FROM film
WHERE title LIKE 'A%' AND description IS NOT NULL

SELECT r.rental_id, r.rental_date
FROM rental AS r
JOIN customer AS c ON c.customer_id = r.customer_id
JOIN inventory AS i ON i.inventory_id = r.inventory_id

SELECT customer_id, amount
FROM payment
WHERE customer_id IS NOT NULL AND amount IS NOT NULL

SELECT c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name, COUNT(*) AS payments
FROM customer AS c
JOIN payment AS p ON p.customer_id = c.customer_id
GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name

SELECT customer_id, last_name
FROM customer
WHERE customer_id IN (SELECT DISTINCT customer_id FROM rental WHERE staff_id = 2)

SELECT f.film_id, f.title, t.description
FROM film AS f
JOIN film_text AS t ON t.film_id = f.film_id
WHERE f.length > 150

SELECT f.film_id, f.title,
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM inventory AS i WHERE i.film_id = f.film_id) AS copies
FROM film AS f
WHERE f.rental_duration = 7
